The commits to reflect, newest first — read each with `git show --stat <sha>` and `git log -1 <sha>` for the full reasoning, then verify the claims against the CURRENT source before writing anything. Never copy a commit message into the document without checking it still describes the code:

A live overcharge: a game server carries both `planId` and `gamePlanId`, is sold at the game plan's flat price, and the shared `renewalQuote` computed from `plan.priceCents` — so `minecraft-mm8w85` ($4.99) would have been billed at its Starter base plan ($8.99) on "Renew now". - `156b6ac` Hardened the post-cutover TLS sweep after its own first live run exposed three defects in it.
- `4ea9790` Promo-basis proration (`Server.termPromoPercent`), the post-cutover TLS sweep, and eight more migration-rehearsal defects.

=============== 2d8fedd ===============
2d8fedd33df1353ca5b4e8ea24cd8cabbf0c5747
Game servers renew at their game plan price, not the base VPS plan

A live overcharge, and one I introduced earlier today.

`minecraft-mm8w85` is sold at $4.99 — its game plan's flat price — and is
built on a Starter base plan at $8.99. A game server carries BOTH a
`planId` and a `gamePlanId`. The `renewalQuote` I added this morning to
fix the "+30 days" bug was written as fresh arithmetic over
`plan.priceCents`, so it never looked at `gamePlan`: pressing "Renew now"
would have charged that customer $8.99 for a $4.99 product, an 80%
overcharge, and their invoice would have read "Starter VPS" for a
Minecraft server.

`renewalCharge` (lib/stripe-cards.ts) had handled game plans correctly all
along, and the automatic renewal sweep in worker/billing.ts already used
it. So the defect was never a wrong formula — it was a SECOND formula,
which is the same thing that caused the bug I was fixing when I wrote it.

`renewalQuote` now owns no arithmetic at all. It delegates to
`renewalCharge` and adds only the duration phrasing the UI needs; a test
asserts the file contains no price arithmetic of its own. renewNow, the
server page and the wizard's term cards all price through the one
function, and renewal invoice descriptions now use the quote's own label,
so a game server's invoice names the game plan instead of the base VPS.

lib/renewal-charge.ts — extracted, and NOT cosmetic. `renewalCharge` lived
in lib/stripe-cards.ts, which imports the Stripe SDK and transitively
nodemailer. The moment the deploy wizard (a client component) needed the
renewal price, that chain dragged `nodemailer/lib/dkim` into the browser
bundle and the build failed with "Can't resolve 'fs'". Typecheck passed
throughout — only `next build` caught it, which is the argument for
building before deploying rather than trusting tsc. The rule is pure
arithmetic and now lives in a module carrying only the two tiny imports it
needs; stripe-cards re-exports it so no server-side caller changed.

Verified the guard bites: reintroducing the defect (passing gamePlan: null
into renewalCharge) turns the suite red.

tsc clean, 291 tests pass, build clean, deployed and verified live.

f28f15eed3db1c689c4daf04765052fdaed510a3
Refuse truncated Stripe metadata; one quote per order; honest receipt

Three silent-failure bugs on the payment path, all found by reading the
code rather than by a customer complaining.

1. A TRUNCATED ORDER INTENT BECAME A SILENT WALLET TOP-UP.
   Every metadata payload was written `JSON.stringify(x).slice(0, 490)`.
   A slice through JSON is not JSON: the consumer's JSON.parse throws
   inside a try that returns null, so fulfilCheckoutSession could not see
   an order, a resize or a disk expansion in the session and fell through
   to its plain top-up branch. The card was charged, the money landed in
   the wallet, NO server was created, no error was shown and no failure
   row was written — invisible from every surface we own.

   The correct behaviour was already argued for twenty lines away, about
   the card leg: "Refuse to open a session rather than take the money and
   discover it at confirm time — nothing has been charged at this point."
   That reasoning is now applied to the payloads too. `packMetadata`
   throws BEFORE checkout.sessions.create, so the customer fails on a page
   where they have paid nothing. All three payloads (order, resize, disk
   expansion) carried the same latent bug; all three are fixed. A test
   asserts no `.slice(` can reappear inside a metadata block.

2. ONE QUOTE, ONE PRICE. payAndDeploy computed a quote for the wallet
   split, then let createOrderCheckout re-quote internally microseconds
   later from its own `new Date()`. Same function, so no formula could
   drift — but two instants. A promo boundary falling between them would
   price the card leg and the stamped total against different worlds, and
   the wallet would silently absorb the difference. The quote is now
   handed over explicitly.

3. THE RECEIPT PROMISED AN ATTACHMENT IT NEVER SENT. The template said "A
   copy of your invoice is attached for your records" unconditionally,
   while lib/mailer.ts only attaches when the caller passes an invoiceId —
   and the payment-receipt send site passed none. Rather than delete the
   promise, the promise is now kept: the top-up invoice's id is recovered
   from its position in the transaction batch and handed to sendMail, so
   the attachment genuinely ships. Where no invoice exists (a purchase leg
   issues none — the order does), the copy points at billing history
   instead. The flag defaults to FALSE so a caller who forgets it sends a
   receipt that is merely terse, never one that lies.

test/checkout-metadata.test.ts pins all three, including the exact 500/501
boundary. Each tripwire was verified to bite by reverting the fix in place
and confirming the suite goes red.

Also updated one needle in test/purchase-consent.test.ts that pinned the
old inline JSON.stringify shape. The property it guards is unchanged and
stronger: the total is still stamped, and now it cannot be stamped
half-written.

tsc clean, 289 tests pass, build clean, deployed and verified live.

=============== 3aa24d7 ===============
3aa24d74d02417b329c2b0699c85d39931d2dba2
Verification gates, auth lockouts, email verification (gate ships OFF)

Three agents' work, landed together. Two were killed mid-task by an API
limit; the tree they left compiles clean and passes, and what follows is
what I verified rather than what they intended.

AUTH — two ways customers were locked out of their own accounts.
- Anyone who enabled 2FA was locked out PERMANENTLY. The login email
  input was uncontrolled while the password beside it was controlled, and
  React 19 resets uncontrolled fields on every form-action submit: correct
  credentials -> server asks for the code -> React blanks the email ->
  validation fails on the empty email -> the response drops needs2fa ->
  the code field unmounts. No way through, ever.
- A capitalised address made password reset silently impossible. Register
  and login stored/queried verbatim, Postgres @unique is case-sensitive,
  forgot-password lowercased first. `Alice@Example.com` never matched and
  the correctly non-enumerating reply still said a link was on its way.
  Mobile keyboards capitalise the first letter, so this hit real signups.
  Now canonicalised in one place (lib/email-normalize.ts).
- The register error named a rule the password already satisfied and wiped
  the form. It now says what is actually wrong.

EMAIL VERIFICATION — shipped, and deliberately NOT ARMED.
Schema is additive and nullable; `emailVerifiedAt` is pointedly NOT
backfilled, because stamping a timestamp on an address nobody confirmed
would fabricate the one fact the column exists to record. Accounts that
predate the feature are exempted by creation date instead.

I added a third fail-open the agents did not: `email_verification_enforced`
defaults to FALSE. The gate makes "our email arrived" a precondition for
taking money, and `dkim._domainkey.nxeon.cloud` is currently NXDOMAIN, so
every transactional email this platform sends is unsigned. Armed tonight,
a new customer's link lands in spam and they simply cannot buy — and
nothing reports it. A sale lost in silence is worse than the unverified
signups the gate prevents. It is checked BEFORE the mail-transport probe
so disabling it is unconditional, and it is a separate knob from
VERIFICATION_ENFORCED_FROM on purpose: that date is a historical fact
about this database and must never become tunable.

NAT — syncPortForwards no longer flushes the chain.
It opened with an unconditional `iptables -t nat -F NXEON_FWD` and rebuilt
in a loop, so any mid-loop abort left every customer on the box with no
forwarding at all, and nothing checked the result. It now reads the chain,
diffs against intent, applies only the delta, and PROVES the outcome by
re-reading what the kernel actually holds — not that each command exited
0. Port collisions and unbuildable rules are named instead of silently
built over, and rules this engine did not write are reported and left
alone. Verified on the live chain: `verified: 1 rule(s) present (+0/-0)`,
chain byte-identical afterwards, a real customer's SSH forward untouched.

Also: websiteCreate now proves it serves before saying so; backups, SSL
and game auto-update gained real proof (game auto-update previously could
not fail — every branch was `|| true` and it ended `; true`, so it had
reported success unattended every 6 hours regardless of outcome); footer
status, support promises and consent/mobile dead ends addressed.

tsc clean, 282 tests pass, build clean, deployed and verified live.

=============== 156b6ac ===============
156b6acf80de0b3a5c5d413358cdfc0fce11982a
Harden the post-cutover TLS sweep against its own first live run

Deploying the sweep found three defects in it that no test would have.
All three are the same mistake: a background nicety behaving as though it
were the only thing the platform is doing.

1. A PERMANENT error was retried as if transient, and notified every
   time. `readSiteSpec` returning null means the run published no site
   configuration — no amount of waiting or DNS movement makes one appear.
   The first live sweep sent 3 notifications in under two seconds, and
   would have sent 56 per migration over the 14-day window, about
   certificates for sites that do not exist. MigrationTlsResult now
   carries `permanent`, which settles the migration silently. A genuinely
   transient error still retries but notifies ONCE.

2. Four migrations pointed at ONE server, so the sweep opened four
   redundant SSH sessions to the same box. A customer who retries a
   migration three times has three rows and one machine. Now one pass per
   target server, newest first — that run's site config is the one
   actually on disk.

3. Worst: it could wedge the queue. This worker is strictly serial, and
   an unresponsive target left a TLS job RUNNING through two reap cycles
   with everything else waiting behind it. On a hosting platform that is
   a new customer's provisioning job stuck behind a certificate retry for
   a server that is not answering. The pass now has a 4-minute ceiling
   and only ever targets servers in RUNNING state.

Verified on the live queue rather than asserted: jobs drain (4 DONE, the
wedged one reaped to FAILED), the permanent path settles

prorateDeltaCents defaulted its rate basis to currentPromo(now), so a
customer could upgrade during a 45% sale and downgrade during a 15% one
and keep the spread: measured at $207.36 per cycle, repeatable. The rate
a term was actually sold at is now persisted on Server.termPromoPercent
and both halves of every proration read it, so a round trip nets zero by
construction.
- Float, not Int: blending a renewal into a part-used term lands on
  halves (36mo at 45% + 36mo at list = exactly 22.5%), and rounding to 23
  shaved $7.20 off a $1,071.36 credit, compounding per renewal.
- A percent, not a $/mo rate: proration is a DIFFERENCE between two
  plans, so a stored cents figure prices only the plan being left and the
  other half still needs a basis invented for it — which is the bug.
- Renewals BLEND rather than overwrite. Overwriting to 0 re-rates a
  still-running 45%-off term to list: $311.04 handed back on a 72-month
  window.
- Backfill uses the deepest catalogue promo as the floor, NOT the
  undiscounted price. A credit is monotonically increasing in the rate
  basis, so the undiscounted fallback emits the LARGEST credit the
  function can produce — $168.84 of cash never spent, plus three years of
  running VPS. Being wrong toward the floor can only make an upgrade
  cheaper; it can never push cash out. 4 rows, all 4 recovered from real
  billing records against the cash actually taken, 0 fallbacks used.
- adminExtendServer records gifted months at 100% off and blends, so the
  cash value of the paid window is unchanged: a customer who bought 12
  months and was gifted a 13th still gets back what the 12 are worth.
  Zeroing would confiscate; leaving the rate alone was the money printer.

worker/migrate.ts — the post-cutover certificate pass is no longer dead.
runPostCutoverTls had exactly one enqueue line and it was INSIDE A
COMMENT, so a customer who pointed DNS a day after migrating never got
the certificate that could not be issued during the run — their first
HTTPS visit was a browser warning, permanently. sslSweep does not cover
this: it walks db.sslCertificate rows and a migration never writes one.
This was made worse the same day by the new cutover copy promising
"Nxeon issues the certificate automatically within about 30 minutes",
which was false the moment it shipped. postCutoverTlsSweep now watches
terminal migrations for 14 days, retries at most every 6 hours, and marks
items.tlsSettled once nothing is outstanding. A promise the product does
not keep is the same defect as a success it did not verify.

worker/migrate-real.ts — eight more rehearsal defects, all one root cause
(clean() destroying row structure before a line/column parse):
- The stale-reference sweep skipped 100% of lines (its first statement
  was `indexOf("\t") < 0 → continue`) and then reported a clean bill of
  health from parsing zero lines. SWEEP_OK was already being printed and
  had never been read; it now gates that claim.
- Database accounts: every run carrying DB users pushed failed, "none of
  the 3 could be recreated", while all three worked. Now that failed
  steps drive the outcome, this alone downgraded every such migration.
- Listening ports: the $-anchored regex over glued output matched only
  the LAST port on the box, so a container app that was up got no vhost
  and its domain served the stock distro page.

  ssl flags, so a site that was plain HTTP there and still is is reported

=============== fd71056 ===============
fd710567670c6b4f4332a16ac94456cba6aff381
Migration rehearsal fixes, proration symmetry, wallet floor, CI

The first real end-to-end migration rehearsal found eleven defects. The
severe ones all shared one shape: a verification step that read corrupted
input and reported success.

worker/migrate-real.ts
- clean() strips [\x00-\x1f], which includes \n and \t, and six
  verification paths then .split("\n") the result. Added cleanLines() and
  switched the broken sites. The worst was resolvesHere(): every A record
  collapsed into one string, so .includes(ip) was ALWAYS false — a domain
  correctly pointed at the new server was reported as not pointing there,
  which gates HTTP-01, so certificate issuance was unreachable. The same
  bug made unitState() report a healthy unit as "activeSubState/running"
  and left NRestarts unparseable, so the crash-loop detector could never
  fire. systemctl keys are now anchored per line.
- The docker inspect Go template aborted on {{len .HostConfig.Devices}};
  docker then writes nothing and exits non-zero, so with 2>/dev/null the
  container vanished from the inventory entirely. Guarded, and the
  inventory now carries an authoritative `docker ps -aq | wc -l` count so
  a shortfall is a blocker instead of reading as "no containers".
- parseInventory() filtered out containers whose name/image failed
  validation, which made planContainer's own "not reproducible safely"
  blockers unreachable. They are now carried through and named.
- The server_name harvest swept all of /etc/nginx with no filter, so
  commented-out lines and un-symlinked sites-available entries became
  domains the source "answered on" — phantom names in the score's
  denominator, which made a COMPLETED outcome unreachable. Now enabled
  config only, directive anchored to the start of its line.
- /home is in DEFAULT_PATHS *and* in UNSAFE_EXACT, so the default
  selection shown to every customer was silently discarded. It is now
  expanded into per-user directories with collisions named, and any
  refused path is reported rather than dropped.
- preflightUnitExecs symlinked a missing interpreter to whatever the
  target had and called it "the same program" without comparing versions.
  Node 20 -> Node 12 stops the 203/EXEC and starts a runtime failure,
  which reads as a successful repair. Major versions are now compared;
  a mismatch blocks with the right install command. An unreadable
  version is never compared — a false mismatch misleads too.
- judgeMigrationOutcome ignored steps with status "failed" entirely: a
  failed database restore could score COMPLETED. It now takes failedSteps
  and unreadContainers.
- The report gave contradictory DNS instructions ("point the DNS, then
  run certbot" vs "do not move DNS for these names yet") with no way to
  tell which applied to which name. One explicit ordered cutover block
  replaces both, and certificate issuance is stated as automatic.
- srcInventoryScript is exported so its ~120 lines of generated shell can
  be parsed by sh -n and dash -n in the test suite. Three nested levels
  of quoting fail on a customer's live server, not in a build.

Money
- lib/proration.ts: removed capMonths. Two servers and two client
  pickers had to agree on it by convention and did not, so an
  upgrade-then-downgrade round trip kept $362.88 on a stacked expiry.
  The optional knob was the defect; now nobody can express a different
  duration. Uncapped is correct both ways — expiresAt only advances
  against payment.
- lib/wallet-split.ts: a due under the 50c Stripe minimum returned a
  sub-floor card leg with clampedForStripeMin false, handed straight to
  Stripe by two actions. Now the wallet takes it and belowStripeMin says
  so; the customer never owes more than the quote.
- MigrationWizard: named Docker volume bytes were detected and never
  quoted, so the engine demanded more disk than the customer was told.
  Added to the Docker allowance, not the files total (the reverse error
  cost ~40GB once).

Tests and CI
- .github/workflows/ci.yml: typecheck + tests on push and PR.
- tsconfig allowImportingTsExtensions, so `npm run check` can pass at
  all — bare tsc always exited 1 on TS5097.
- 129 tests pass, typecheck clean.

Stop charging customers without consent; card-save UI

A full customer-journey rehearsal on staging found three launch blockers,
all reproduced in a browser, all byte-identical in production. Each is
the same shape: what the customer sees is not what the system does. That
is the defect class this session spent its day removing from the
migration engine — here it arrives on the purchase path, where instead of
misreporting a server it takes money.

1. THE WIZARD CHARGED FOUR STEPS EARLY. Clicking "Continue →" on the
   Access step placed the order outright, at the default monthly term,
   before any total or Review screen. Reproduced five times: five servers
   created, five wallet debits, no price ever shown. Cause: Continue and
   Deploy were two branches of an UNKEYED ternary at the same position in
   the tree, so React reconciled them as ONE DOM node — advancing the step
   swapped Continue's type="button" for the Deploy branch's absent type,
   the live node became a submit control mid-click, and the browser
   submitted. The pre-existing guard only ever covered the Enter key,
   while asserting in its own comment that "Deploy only ever happens via
   the explicit button". Fixed at the cause (distinct keys, explicit
   types on both) and given a real net: the form refuses to submit
   anywhere but the Review step, so a charge without consent no longer
   depends on getting JSX reconciliation right.

2. "Renew now (+30 days, $8.99)" CHARGED $97.09 AND ADDED 12 MONTHS.
   The label hardcoded the string "+30 days" and the plan's MONTHLY
   price; renewNow has always charged vpsTermPriceCents for termMonths.
   10.8x on Starter/12mo, 28.8x on Max/36mo, no confirmation between the
   click and the debit. lib/renewal-quote.ts is now the single definition
   of what renewal costs and buys — the action charges through it and the
   page quotes through it, so they cannot drift. Same remedy as
   lib/proration.ts, for the same reason. Plus one confirmation naming
   the real amount and the real duration.

3. THE PROMO BAR ADVERTISED A PRICE NOBODY COULD BUY. "VPS from $5 →
   $3.50/mo", live on every marketing page, while the same page rendered
   the real $8.99. The file hardcoded exampleRegular = 500 under a
   comment reading "our entry VPS regularly bills $5/mo", and its docblock
   claimed the component was "honest by construction" and that the
   headline "matches what checkout charges". It now reads the cheapest
   active plan from the catalogue, renders cents (>$8.99 as "$9" is a
   smaller false claim, not a true one), and renders NOTHING rather than
   invent a price when no plan is sellable. Verified live: the bar now
   reads "VPS from $8.99 $6.29/mo, renews at $8.99/mo".

CARD-SAVE UI — the launch blocker I had wrongly marked complete.
lib/actions-payment-method.ts had zero importers, so no customer could
save a card and every renewal was wallet-only: an empty wallet went
straight to grace → suspend, exactly what the dunning engine exists to
prevent. components/customer/PaymentMethod.tsx + the billing page now
cover add/replace/remove, the Stripe return leg, settle-now, and the
customer's real position in the dunning ladder (derived from
DUNNING_RETRY_ATTEMPTS, never hardcoded). With no card on file the panel
says 0 attempts, not 4 — the worker genuinely never attempts anything,
and claiming otherwise would be the most misleading thing it could say.
The wallet-vs-card preference is deliberately UNCHANGED: the card funds
the wallet and the wallet pays the bill, one money path, and flipping the
worker alone would make settleOutstanding's quote disagree with the
charge.

test/purchase-consent.test.ts pins all three blockers. The source
tripwires strip comments before matching — every fix here quotes its own
bug in a comment, and a guard that matches its own incident note fails on
correct code, which teaches people to ignore it. Each tripwire was
verified to bite by reverting the fix in a scratch copy.

tsc clean, 174 tests pass, build clean, deployed and confirmed live.

1	# Nxeon — the internal manual
2	
3	The single reference for how this platform actually works: what each feature does, which file does
4	it, how it fails, and how you diagnose it at 3am. Rendered privately at **`/admin/docs`**, which
5	splits this file into searchable sections at every `##` heading.
6	
7	**Read this first.** Three rules govern the whole document:
8	
9	1. **Reference leads, history follows.** Parts I–VII are reference. The dated change log is Part
10	   VIII, at the bottom, kept verbatim.
11	2. **Every `file:line` here was opened and read.** Line numbers drift as several agents edit this
12	   tree concurrently — treat them as "this function, roughly here", and grep the quoted symbol if a
13	   number has slipped.
14	3. **This manual does not overclaim.** The single recurring defect in this codebase is *a surface
15	   reporting an outcome it never verified*. A manual that asserted features work because the code
16	   looks complete would be that same bug in a new place. Where something is simulated, partial, or
17	   saved-and-never-read, the chapter says so, and **Known gaps — the honest inventory** collects
18	   every instance.
19	
20	Companion documents — read them, do not edit them:
21	
22	| File | What it is |
23	|---|---|
24	| `docs/AUDIT-24H.md` | Line-by-line verification of a 24-hour engineering session against the live tree. Its "top 10 gaps" is the best map of trust debt in this repo. |
25	| `docs/QA-PRELAUNCH.md` | Pre-launch QA sweep. Source of the cross-tenant email-takeover finding. |
26	| `docs/MIGRATION-FIELD-NOTES.md` | 28 numbered real-world migration failures with the fix for each. Acceptance criteria for the migration engine. |
27	| `docs/MIGRATION.md` | Moving the Nxeon *platform itself* to another box — not customer migration. |
28	| `CLAUDE.md` | Agent-facing conventions and safety rules. |
29	| `ROADMAP.md` | Known to be wrong in both directions. See Known gaps before trusting it. |
30	
31	---
32	
33	## What Nxeon is
34	
35	Nxeon is a self-hosted, Hostinger-style VPS hosting business. A visitor lands on the marketing site,
36	picks a plan and a term, pays, and about ninety seconds later has root on a real KVM virtual
37	machine — plus, from the same portal, domains, TLS, mailboxes, block storage, backups, game servers,
38	a web console, an AI build assistant, and a one-click lift-and-shift migration from whatever host
39	they are leaving.
40	
41	It all runs on **one** dedicated server:
42	
43	- **Hypervisor**: Proxmox VE 9 on an OVH KS-GAME (i7-7700K, 64 GB RAM). Storage is a 2×450 GB NVMe
44	  ZFS mirror (pool `data`, 358 G) for live VM disks and a 4 TB HDD pool (`tank`, 3.6 T) for backups.
45	- **Guests**: customer VMs cloned from cloud-init templates VMID 9000–9009, plus VMID **8000
46	  `nxeon-mail`** — the Mailcow appliance carrying every mailbox on the platform: the transactional
47	  sender *and* paid customer business email.
48	- **Web, worker and Postgres run on the Proxmox host itself**, not in a VM.
49	
50	The product surface, in one view:
51	
52	```
53	 MARKETING  app/(marketing)        CUSTOMER PORTAL  app/dashboard      ADMIN  app/admin
54	 ──────────────────────────        ───────────────────────────────     ──────────────────
55	 /  pricing  vps  domains          servers   deploy    migrate         servers   users
56	 game-servers  business-email      volumes   ssl       domains         plans     products
57	 block-storage  migrate            mail      calendar  email           invoices  billing
58	 vibe-coding  compare  blog        games     build     claude-code     jobs  nodes  ips
59	 tools/*  (12 free tools)          billing   invoices  team            domains   mail
60	 legal/*  status  help             support   settings  refer           support   abuse
61	                                   projects  activity  feedback        docs      settings
62	```
63	
64	Three properties to internalise before you touch anything:
65	
66	- **Nothing mutates a VM from the web tier.** Every state change is a `Job` row the worker picks up.
67	  The web app may *read* Proxmox freely; it may not write. This is why "I clicked the button and
68	  nothing happened" is nearly always a worker question, not a web question.
69	- **One in-flight job per server, and the worker is strictly serial.** A 24-minute migration blocks
70	  every other customer's SSL issuance behind it. That is a real, unfixed design limit — see Known
71	  gaps.
72	- **Money is integer cents everywhere.** `balanceCents`, `priceCents`, `amountCents`. There are no
73	  floats in the billing path.
74	
75	## Architecture at a glance

3705	displayed-vs-charged pricing, migration sizing, disk expansion, the wallet split, or the migration
3706	verification gate.
3707	
3708	---
3709	
3710	# Part VI — Honest status
3711	
3712	## The recurring defect — reporting an outcome nobody verified
3713	
3714	**This codebase has one bug, and it has shipped many times.** A surface reports an outcome it never
3715	verified. Every variant below is the same shape:
3716	
3717	```
3718	 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
3719	 │  do something  ──►  ASSUME it worked  ──►  write success             │
3720	 │                                            notify the customer       │
3721	 │                                            render it as fact         │
3722	 └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
3723	                    ▲
3724	                    └── the missing step: ASK THE WORLD WHETHER IT WORKED
3725	```
3726	
3727	Five instances found on a single day:
3728	
3729	| Instance | What was claimed | What was true |
3730	|---|---|---|
3731	| SSL | Certificate rows `ACTIVE` with a `now + 90d` expiry and *"Your Let's Encrypt certificate is active"* | No certbot ran. No certificate existed anywhere on the box |
3732	| Game settings | *"Game settings applied on `<hostname>`"* | Nothing was written to the VM; the `(sandbox)` qualifier was suppressed because `SANDBOX` is false in production |
3733	| Migration | `Sites actually serving: 4/4` | Six of the customer's domains were dark. The denominator was "domains we chose to publish", so the metric was 100% **by construction** |
3734	| Domain markup | Admin panel displayed **0%** | Customers were charged **25%**. Nothing read the setting at all |
3735	| Auto-suspend kill switch | An admin toggle that appeared to be saved | It was saved, and read by nothing |
3736	
3737	**The four shapes to watch for**, because they recur:
3738	
3739	1. **Simulated-success fall-through.** A feature flag is unset, so the code takes a branch that writes
3740	   the success value without doing the work.
3741	2. **Saved-but-unread.** An admin sets a value; nothing consumes it. Worse when a panel *states* what
3742	   it affects.
3743	3. **Env-vs-setting split.** The value is read from `process.env` while the admin edits a `Setting`
3744	   row (or vice versa). Both the domain markup and `referral_reward_cents` are this.
3745	4. **A metric that cannot fail.** A denominator chosen from the numerator's own set; a shell command
3746	   ending `; true`; a status written outside the `if` that decided it.
3747	
3748	**Two things this project got right, and they are the pattern to copy:**
3749	
3750	- **Fail loudly instead of simulating.** `worker/ssl.ts:692` and `worker/game-config.ts:86` now
3751	  *throw* with an explanation naming the flag, rather than writing a success. The customer sees a
3752	  failure with a real reason. That is strictly better than a comforting lie, even though it means the
3753	  feature is visibly unavailable.
3754	- **Delete the control you cannot enforce.** `Membership.areas` was written, echoed back as saved, and
3755	  read by nothing. Rather than leave it, the control was **removed** and the customer is told what a
3756	  membership actually grants (`lib/actions-teams.ts:22-26`).
3757	
3758	And the meta-lesson, from `docs/MIGRATION-FIELD-NOTES.md:115-127`, about failure #25 recurring four
3759	months after it was written up as #13 in the same file:
3760	
3761	> **A documented fix is not a fix. Nothing in the engine read this file.** … a failure mode that has
3762	> been observed twice belongs in code, and a field note describing a fix nobody implemented is worth
3763	> approximately nothing.
3764	
3765	Which is why **this manual is not a substitute for a check**. If you find yourself documenting a
3766	behaviour rather than asserting it, ask whether a test or a guard would be a better place to put the
3767	sentence.
3768	
3769	## Known gaps — the honest inventory
3770	
3771	Every entry below was re-opened and re-checked against the tree on **2026-07-26 at commit `fd71056`**,
3772	after the first end-to-end migration rehearsal. Several agents edit this repo concurrently — at the
3773	moment of that pass `worker/migrate-real.ts`, `lib/proration.ts`, `lib/resize.ts`,
3774	`lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts`, `lib/promotions.ts` and `prisma/schema.prisma` all had uncommitted
3775	edits in flight, and `worker/migrate-real.ts` alone moved ~436 lines that day. **Line numbers in that
3776	file drift by the hour.** When a citation misses, grep the quoted symbol rather than assuming the claim
3777	is stale — and correct the number here when you do. Classification:
3778	
3779	- **WORKS** — verified end to end.
3780	- **SIMULATED** — produces a fabricated result.
3781	- **UNVERIFIED SUCCESS** — does real work but reports success without checking it.
3782	- **SAVED-BUT-UNREAD** — written by a UI, consumed by nothing.
3783	- **DEAD** — implemented, never called.
3784	- **PARTIAL** — real but incomplete or overstated.

3822	#### Found by the first end-to-end migration rehearsal — 2026-07-26, commit `fd71056`
3823	
3824	The engine had never been run against a purpose-built messy source. It was, and it broke in nine
3825	places, none of which any existing test or type would have caught. **Line numbers in
3826	`worker/migrate-real.ts` move constantly — grep the symbol, not the number.**
3827	
3828	| Item | Evidence |
3829	|---|---|
3830	| **`clean()` deleted the newlines six verification paths then split on** | `clean` (`migrate-real.ts:363`) strips `\n` and `\t` — correct for a hostname, wrong for anything parsed by line. Six callers did `clean(...).split("\n")` and got a single element containing the whole output concatenated, so the parse produced nothing while the surrounding code reported success. `cleanLines` (`:396`) now sits beside it, preserving `\n`/`\t`; both carry the incident note. Fixed at `resolvesHere` (`:3331`), the `df` tail (`:1534`) and `unitState`'s `systemctl show` parse (`:2843`, which now anchors each `KEY=value` with `^…$`/`m`). **Two consequences were severe:** `resolvesHere()` was **always false**, so a domain correctly pointed at the new server read as not pointing there and HTTP-01 issuance was unreachable; and `NRestarts` parsed to `NaN`, so field note 26's crash-loop detector could never fire |
3831	| **A Go template aborted and containers vanished from the inventory** | `{{len .HostConfig.Devices}}` on its own aborts the **whole** `docker inspect` template on "len of nil pointer" — docker then writes nothing and exits non-zero, so under `2>/dev/null` the container produced zero lines and disappeared. Guarded at `migrate-real.ts:947`. Backed by an authoritative `docker ps -aq` piped to `wc -l`, emitted as `CCOUNT` (`:965-966`, parsed at `:1112`), so a shortfall is now a named discrepancy (`containersUnread`, `:3850`) instead of reading as "no containers" |
3832	| **`parseInventory` deleted the containers `planContainer` existed to flag** | The commit line used to `.filter((c) => CONTNAME_RE.test(c.name) && validImageRef(c.image))`, so `planContainer`'s own "name is not reproducible safely" / "image reference is not reproducible safely" blockers were **unreachable** — the parser threw those containers away before the planner saw them, and a container the customer was running simply ceased to exist in the report. Now every container survives (`:1281`) and the unreproducible ones are listed as `containersUnreadable` (`:1285`); the recreate loop still refuses to act on an unvalidated name/image |
3833	| **The `server_name` harvest scanned comments and disabled vhosts** | It was `grep -rhoE 'server_name…' /etc/nginx` over the entire tree, so `# server_name old.example.com;` became a domain "the source answered on" and entered the **denominator** the final score is measured against — a name the old server never served can never serve here, so `COMPLETED` was unreachable. `sites-available/` was swept even when not symlinked into `sites-enabled/`, adding `.bak`/`.dpkg-dist` leftovers. Now anchored to the start of a line and restricted to enabled paths (`:997-1021`), with the trailing `;` and inline `#` stripped by name rather than by a blind `.slice(1)` (`:1197-1203`) |
3834	| **`/home` — the default selection — was silently discarded** | `/home` is in `DEFAULT_PATHS` (`lib/actions-migrate.ts:110`) **and** in `UNSAFE_EXACT` (`migrate-real.ts:327`), so `safeCopyTarget` refused it and a `.filter()` in the validation preamble dropped it without a word. 3835	| **The exec pre-flight called Node 12 "the same program" as Node 20** | `preflightUnitExecs` (`:2728`) symlinked a missing interpreter to whatever it found and reported a repair, without ever comparing versions — turning a `203/EXEC` into a runtime failure that looks like a successful fix and is harder to diagnose. It now compares majors via `majorVersion()` (`:2717`) and `UnitExecHost.versionOf` / `versionOnSource`, and a mismatch is a **blocker** carrying the right install command (`:2774-2792`) |
3836	| **`judgeMigrationOutcome` ignored failed steps** | A run could fail to restore a database, fail to pull an image and fail to start a container and still score `COMPLETED`, because those failures were neither domains nor units. === QA-JOURNEY head ===
# QA — Full customer journey rehearsal

**Date:** 2026-07-26
**Environment driven:** staging (`nxeon-staging-web` :3001, nginx :8080 / `https://staging.nxeon.cloud`, DB `nxeon_staging`, `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`)
**Production touched:** read-only `GET` on public marketing pages only. No Stripe charge, no VM create/destroy, no DNS/OVH change, no outbound mail to a real person.

---

## 0. Method, and a caveat that affects how you read this

Every finding below is tagged:

- **[RAN]** — I drove it over real HTTP/a real browser and watched it happen.
- **[READ]** — I traced the code path and did not execute it. Never presented as an observed result.

Test accounts created on staging: `dana.quill2@example.com`, `sam.card@example.com`, `sam.two@example.com`. Six sandbox servers and ~$1,500 of play money. All disposable.

### Caveat: staging is 21 commits behind production

`/opt/nxeon-staging` is at `8c8b7d9`; `/opt/nxeon` is at `fd71056`. Twenty-one commits apart, including several that touch exactly what I was asked to test (wallet floor, proration symmetry, Stripe-provision coupling, coupons, notification prefs, sidebar).

So for **every** finding I observed on staging I diffed the responsible file against the production tree and said which applies. Where the file is byte-identical I say so explicitly. **This staleness is itself a launch-readiness problem**: the environment built to rehearse the release does not contain the release. Re-run `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` before trusting staging for anything else.

---

## LAUNCH BLOCKERS

### B1. The wizard charges the customer when they click "Continue →", four steps before the confirmation screen

**[RAN]** — reproduced 5 times, 5 servers created, 5 wallet debits.
`components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx:646-661` — **byte-identical in staging and production.**

On the **Access** step, type a valid hostname and click **Continue →**. Instead of advancing to Review, the order is placed immediately: a `Next-Action` POST to `payAndDeploy`, wallet debited, VM provisioned, browser redirected to the new server's page.

The customer never sees the Review step. They never choose a billing term (it commits at the `default_term`, currently Monthly). They never see "Due today". There is no confirmation of any kind between clicking a button labelled *Continue* and money leaving their wallet.

Verified ledger from one such click:

```
-629  Order: Starter VPS (qa-probe-02) — Monthly · Summer Sale 30% off first term
```

**Root cause** (**[READ]**, following from the observed behaviour): the two buttons are branches of an unkeyed ternary in the same DOM position.

```jsx
{!isLast ? (
  <button type="button" ... onClick={() => setStep((s) => s + 1)}>Continue →</button>
) : (
  <button className="btn-primary px-6" disabled={pending || !canDeploy} ...>   // no type → submit
)}
```

React reconciles both branches onto the **same `<button>` element** and patches its attributes. `setStep` runs inside the click handler, React re-renders synchronously, and `type="button"` is removed from the very node the browser is still processing the click for. The browser then performs its default action — submit. It only fires when `canDeploy` is true, which is why an **empty** hostname reaches Review correctly and a **filled** one does not. That is the whole bug.

- Wallet-funded customer: **charged with no confirmation screen.**
- Zero-balance card customer **[RAN]**: `payAndDeploy` returns a `checkoutUrl`, but the redirect is gated on `submittedRef` which the Deploy button never got to set — so the redirect is suppressed and the customer lands on Review looking normal. No charge, no visible damage, but a stray Stripe Checkout session per traversal.

**Smallest fix:** add distinct `key` props (`key="continue"` / `key="deploy"`) so React unmounts one and mounts the other, and give the deploy button an explicit `type="submit"`.

---

content.content:
115	## HIGH — money and trust
116	
117	### H1. The term cards state a recurring price that will never be charged
118	
119	**[RAN]** — read verbatim off the running Review step.
120	`components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx:544-563`
121	
122	```
123	−10%  Annual   $5.66/mo   $67.96 billed every 1 yr
124	−20%  Triennial $5.03/mo  $181.24 billed every 3 yr
125	```
126	
127	"$67.96 billed every 1 yr" is the **promo first-term** price. Renewals bill the regular price — `$97.09` — which I confirmed by actually renewing (B2). `currentPromo()` never returns null (`LAUNCH_SALE`, 15%, `lib/promotions.ts:58-65`), so this is wrong on **100% of orders, 100% of the time**.
128	
129	The disclosure below it — *"30% off your first term applied — renews at the regular price"* — carries no number and no date, and the strikethrough regular total appears only on the "Due today" row, not on the card that says *billed every*.
130	
131	`components/marketing/PricingGrid.tsx:110` gets this exactly right (*"First term. Renews at $8.99/mo."*). Copy that.
132	
133	**Smallest fix:** `{money(total)} first term · renews at {money(regTotal)}` — `regTotal` is already in scope at line 544.
134	
135	### H2. Stripe order confirm re-prices after the card is charged and takes the difference from the wallet
136	
137	**[READ]** — `lib/actions.ts:391-430` → `lib/stripe.ts:41` → `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts:70-80` → `lib/order.ts:158,188,197`
138	
139	The Checkout session metadata carries the *intent*, never the quoted total, so `placeOrder` re-runs `orderQuote` at confirm time — including a fresh `currentPromo(new Date())`. If the promo rotates between checkout creation and the Stripe redirect, the recomputed total is debited from the wallet with no new consent. With no balance: payment captured, no server, and a notification reading *"Payment received — we couldn't finish setting up your server."*
140	
141	This is an inconsistency rather than an oversight in principle: `lib/resize.ts:115` and `lib/disk-expand.ts:153` already take the amount from Stripe metadata precisely so confirm cannot re-price. The order path is the one that missed it.
142	
143	**Smallest fix:** add `c: quote.chargeCents` to the `nxeonOrder` metadata and give `placeOrder` an optional `chargeCents` override, mirroring `applyResize`.
144	
145	### H3. A card-paid purchase produces two PAID invoices and doubles "Paid · lifetime"
146	
147	**[READ]** — `lib/stripe.ts:230-239`, `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts:70`, `app/dashboard/invoices/page.tsx:23-25,38`
148	
149	`creditCheckoutSession` writes a PAID *"Wallet top-up"* invoice for every paid session, then the order branch writes its own. An $82.53 annual purchase shows as `Wallet top-up $82.53` + `Starter VPS — Annual $82.53`, and the invoices page reports **$165.06** paid lifetime.
150	
151	Each document is internally consistent (`lib/invoices.ts:139-163` derives totals from line items), so nothing is fabricated — but a customer reconciling against their card statement sees twice their spend. `worker/billing.ts:615-617` already states the correct rule for the renewal path.
152	
153	**[RAN] counter-check:** for **wallet-paid** orders and renewals the invoices reconcile *exactly* with the ledger — 7 invoices, 7 wallet rows, amounts identical including the $97.09 renewal. The defect is specific to the Stripe leg.
154	
155	### H4. Automatic backups can silently never exist while the UI shows a fresh timestamp every night
156	
157	**[READ]** — `worker/backup-schedule.ts:55-61`, `worker/index.ts:745-768,979-985`; customer-facing at `components/customer/BackupSchedule.tsx:103-105`
158	
159	`lastAutoBackup` is stamped **when the job row is enqueued**, not when the backup succeeds — and it is written nowhere else. `backupCreate` gates the vzdump task's exit status but never checks the archive exists or is non-zero, has no failure notification, and is excluded from `VM_STATE_FAILURE_JOBS`.
160	
161	So "Last automatic backup: 2026-07-26 04:00 UTC" means *a row was created*. vzdump could have failed every night for a month with no alert, and the schedule is marked satisfied so the retry is a full interval away. Discovered at restore time — the one moment it cannot be fixed.
162	
163	Aggravating: the deploy wizard **sells** this at the point of sale (**[RAN]** — Add-ons step reads *"Daily auto-backups · Included · Nightly snapshots to separate storage for easy restore"*).
164	
165	**Smallest fix:** drop the `lastAutoBackup` write in `backup-schedule.ts` (the in-flight de-dupe at :50-53 already prevents pile-up) and set it in `backupCreate` after a storage-content read shows a fresh volid with `size > 0`. Add a failure `notify`.
166	
167	### H5. `syncPortForwards` flushes the whole NAT chain and rebuilds it unverified
168	
169	**[READ]** — `worker/network.ts:28-55`
170	
171	Line 30 unconditionally runs `iptables -t nat -F NXEON_FWD`, then rebuilds per-server in a loop with no try/catch, no rollback and no `-C` read-back. `exec` here is `promisify(execFile)`, so **one** failed `-A` rejects and aborts the loop — every server after that point is left with no DNAT rule. The job still goes DONE, because DONE means "the last `iptables -A` exited 0".
172	
173	Fleet-wide SSH blackhole, no notification, dashboard still showing everyone's port. `remove()` (`worker/index.ts:401`) calls this *after* deleting the server row, so a throw re-queues DELETE, which then dies on "Server not found" and never retries the sync.
174	
175	**Smallest fix:** build into a scratch chain and swap atomically; at minimum collect per-rule failures instead of aborting, then assert each server's rule with `iptables -t nat -C`.
176

271	## Environments — production, staging, and the .env contract
272	
273	The code is byte-identical between environments. Every difference is an environment variable. That
274	is the entire isolation model, which is why one wrong value in `.env` is how staging would eat
275	production's IP pool.
276	
277	| | Production | Staging |
278	|---|---|---|
279	| Tree | `/opt/nxeon` | `/opt/nxeon-staging` |
280	| Database | `nxeon` | `nxeon_staging` |
281	| Web service | `nxeon-web.service` :3000 | `nxeon-staging-web.service` :3001 |
282	| Worker | `nxeon-worker.service` | `nxeon-staging-worker.service` |
283	| Terminal backend | `nxeon-terminal.service` | `nxeon-terminal-staging.service` |
284	| Console proxy | `nxeon-console-proxy.service` | `nxeon-staging-console-proxy.service` |
285	| VM IP pool | `10.20.0.100–250` | `10.20.0.50–99` |
286	| SSH DNAT ports | `20000–29999` | `30000–30999` |
287	| iptables chain | `NXEON_FWD` | `NXEON_FWD_STG` |
288	| Proxmox VM tag | *(none)* | `nxeon-staging` |
289	| Admin credentials | `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt` | `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt` |
290	
291	The variables that create the split: `NXEON_ENV`, `NXEON_COOKIE_NAME`, `NXEON_NAT_CHAIN`,
292	`NXEON_TAG`, `NXEON_IP_START`, `NXEON_IP_END`, `NXEON_SSH_PORT_START`, `NXEON_SSH_PORT_END`,
293	`NXEON_CRED_FILE`, `PORT`, `APP_URL`.
294	
295	**They share one Proxmox node and one ZFS pool.** Nothing but those ranges keeps them apart. Never
296	point staging pools at production ranges, and never `qm destroy` anything that has a `Server` row.
297	
298	```
299	  edit /opt/nxeon ──► git commit ──► post-commit hook auto-pushes to GitHub
300	                                        │
301	                      scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]
302	                                        │  build + prisma db push + restart staging
303	                                        ▼
304	                           verify on STAGING_HOST / :8080
305	                                        │
306	                      scripts/promote-production.sh
307	                                        │  rebuild + restart production
308	                                        ▼
309	                                      live
310	```
311	
312	Domains and TLS are driven from **`/etc/nxeon/domains.env`** — currently `BASE_DOMAIN=nxeon.cloud`,
313	`ADMIN_HOST=4j3d7gkr2wcbi34.revsports.ca` (deliberately unguessable; `/admin` 404s on the customer
314	host), `STAGING_HOST=staging.revsports.ca`, plus `CERTBOT_EMAIL`. To move the platform to a new
315	domain: edit those four values, point DNS at the box, run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It
316	regenerates every vhost, obtains Let's Encrypt certificates, rewrites `APP_URL` in both `.env`
317	files, and restarts web. That is the whole migration.
318

361	One convention worth knowing: **`lib/actions-*.ts` files carry `"use server"`**, so *everything they
362	export becomes a POST endpoint reachable by anyone*. That has bitten this codebase twice — see
363	**Two-factor authentication** for the brute-force oracle it created, and the E352 files-tab error

368	# Part II — Feature chapters
369	
370	Each chapter follows the same shape: **what it does → the customer screen → the workflow →

692	## Renewals, card auto-charge and dunning
693	
694	**What it does.** `worker/billing.ts` is the money engine. Every 10 minutes it warns about upcoming
695	renewals, charges everything that is due, retries failed cards on a fixed schedule, suspends what
696	never pays, and terminates what stays unpaid. It is the largest single behavioural surface in the
697	platform and the one where a mistake costs a customer their data.
698	
699	**Trigger.** No cron and no systemd timer. It is an in-process interval inside the worker loop:
700	`/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts:1042` (`if (Date.now() - lastSweep > 10 * 60_000)`) → `:1045`
701	`billingSweep()` → `:1051` `productRenewalSweep()`.
702	
703	**Phase order** — `billingSweep()` at `/opt/nxeon/worker/billing.ts:219`:
704	
705	```
706	 1  adoptUnclaimedCards(now)          :234   (before any card state is read)
707	 2  T-3d "renews soon" notification   :241   suppressed when the wallet covers it
708	                                             OR a chargeable card exists  :256
709	 3  dueServers(now)                   :280 → renewDueServer() per server  :290
710	 4  terminateOverdue(now, cfg)        :296
711	 5  cardExpirySweep                   :302
712	 6  autoRechargeSweep                 :307
713	 7  domainAutoRenewSweep              :312
714	 8  domainTransferInSweep             :317
715	```
716	
717	`dueServers()` at `:198` selects `isFree: false`, `expiresAt: { lt: now }`,
718	`status: { in: ["RUNNING", "STOPPED"] }`. **Suspended servers are deliberately excluded** — which is
719	the root of the incident described in the next chapter.
720	
721	**Wallet credit first, card for the remainder.** `renewDueServer()` at `/opt/nxeon/worker/billing.ts:327`:
722	
723	```
724	 :346  re-read balance (the loop snapshot is stale after the first debit)
725	 :350  split = walletSplit({ dueCents: renewCents, balanceCents: fresh.balanceCents,
726	                             useWallet: true })
727	        │
728	 :357   ├─ split.cardCents === 0 ────────────► commitRenewal()      wallet only, no Stripe
729	 :364   ├─ cardInPlay ──► attemptCardRenewal({ cardCents: split.cardCents })   :379
730	 :388   └─ no card ─────► log and fall through to grace / suspend
731	```
732	
733	The card **never pays the invoice directly**. `attemptCardRenewal` (`:567`) captures `cardCents` at
734	Stripe, credits that amount to the wallet via `creditOffSessionCharge` (`:598`), then calls
735	`commitRenewal` (`:607`) which debits the **full** `renewCents` from the wallet (`:477`). Net effect
736	is identical and there is exactly one debit path in the system. Rationale at `:545-550`.
737	
738	**Retry days 1 / 3 / 5.** One line, `/opt/nxeon/worker/billing.ts:74`:
739	
740	```
741	const retryDayFor = (retry: number) => 2 * retry - 1;      →  1, 3, 5
742	const LAST_RETRY_DAY   = retryDayFor(DUNNING_RETRY_ATTEMPTS);   :76  → 5
743	const CARD_SUSPEND_DAY = LAST_RETRY_DAY + 1;                    :78  → 6
744	const DUNNING_EXHAUSTED = DUNNING_RETRY_ATTEMPTS + 1;           :80  → 4
745	```
746	
747	`DUNNING_RETRY_ATTEMPTS = 3` lives at `/opt/nxeon/lib/mailer.ts:236`, so the retry ladder and the
748	"attempts remaining" copy in the emails derive from one constant (`lib/mailer.ts:377`).
749	
750	```
751	 day 0            day 1           day 3           day 5           day 6
752	 expiry           retry 1         retry 2         retry 3         SUSPEND
753	   │                │               │               │               │
754	   ▼                ▼               ▼               ▼               ▼
755	 charge          charge          charge          charge         SUSPEND job
756	 declined        declined        declined        declined       suspendReason
757	   │                │               │               │            = "UNPAID"
758	 stage 1         stage 2         stage 3         stage 4            │
759	   │                │               │               │           notification
760	 email:          email:          email:          email:         only — NO email
761	 payment_        payment_        payment_        payment_
762	 failed          retry_failed    retry_failed    final_notice
763	                 (1 left)        (2 left)
764	
765	 … then terminateOverdue at cfg.terminateDays (default 14) past expiry,
766	   with a warning notification at cfg.warnDays (default 7).
767	```
768	
769	`nextRetryAt()` at `:850` schedules `expiresAt + retryDayFor(failures) × DAY`, floored by
770	`MIN_RETRY_GAP_MS = 20h` (`:86`) — so a worker outage cannot burn the whole ladder in one sweep. A
771	**transient** error or a 3-D Secure challenge does *not* consume an attempt: `:650` and `:714` call
772	`rescheduleAttempt()` (`:866`), which writes only `dunningNextAt`.
773	
774	Emails (all from `/opt/nxeon/lib/mailer.ts`): `payment_failed` `:309`, `payment_retry_failed` `:383`,
775	`payment_action_required` `:417`, `payment_final_notice` `:444`, `payment_receipt` `:340`,
776	`card_expiring_soon` `:475`. The receipt is guarded by `if (credited)` at `worker/billing.ts:612` so
777	a replayed capture cannot double-receipt.
778	
779	**Off-session charge safety.** `chargeSavedCardOffSession()` at `/opt/nxeon/lib/stripe-cards.ts:508`
780	has two independent idempotency guards: a **permanent** marker lookup (`findChargeByMarker` at
781	`:482`, matching `pi.metadata.nxeonChargeKey`) and Stripe's own 24-hour `idempotencyKey` (`:582`).
782	Markers: `renew:<serverId>:<periodStart ISO>` (`:472`) and `autorecharge:<userId>:<day>` (`:477`).
783	Error classification defaults to **`transient`** (`:630`) with the reason stated at `:604`: *"a
784	misclassified decline costs a paid-up customer their server."*
785	
786	**Admin knobs** — `dunningConfig()` at `/opt/nxeon/worker/billing.ts:139` reads
787	`dunning_grace_days` (3), `dunning_terminate_days` (14), `dunning_warn_days` (7) and
788	`auto_suspend_enabled` (true) from Settings, with env fallbacks at `:131-137` and clamps at
789	`:151-153`. The `auto_suspend_enabled` kill switch is genuinely read now, in three places:
790	`worker/billing.ts:897`, `:924` (`if (!cfg.autoSuspend) return;`) and `:1316`. Panel:
791	`/opt/nxeon/components/admin/settings/BillingPanel.tsx:24-46`.
792	
793	**Product renewals** — `/opt/nxeon/worker/product-renewals.ts:520` covers `EmailSubscription` and
794	`Volume` on the same tick, with deliberately different policy:
795	
796	| | `worker/billing.ts` | `worker/product-renewals.ts` |
797	|---|---|---|
798	| Subjects | VPS, game servers, domains, transfers, cards | email subscriptions, volumes |
799	| Payment | wallet **+ saved card off-session** | **wallet only** — no Stripe import at all |
800	| Dunning | 4 attempts, days 0/1/3/5, 4 email templates | none — in-portal notifications only |
801	| Enforcement | `SUSPEND` job + `suspendReason: "UNPAID"` | email → `SUSPENDED` (mailboxes kept, `:210`); volume → `DETACHED` (`:391`) |
802	| Deletion | yes, `terminateOverdue` deletes unpaid VMs | **never** — `:34` "Nothing here ever deletes customer data." |
803	| Policy location | inline in the worker | extracted to pure `lib/product-billing.ts` |
804	
805	**Failure modes.**
806	
807	| Mode | Behaviour | Where |
808	|---|---|---|
809	| Wallet short, no card | Falls to grace → suspend at `cfg.graceDays` | `worker/billing.ts:388`, `:911` |
810	| Card declined, hard | Consumes an attempt, email, retry scheduled | `recordDeclinedAttempt` `:733` |
811	| Card declined, transient/network | Reschedules **without** consuming an attempt | `rescheduleAttempt` `:866` |
812	| 3-D Secure required | `payment_action_required` email + hosted `dunningPayUrl` | `:700`, `createOutstandingCheckout` `lib/stripe-cards.ts:721` |
813	| Sweep crashes mid-server | Per-server `try`/`catch` at `:291`; next tick retries | `worker/billing.ts:291` |
814	| Double charge on retry | Impossible — marker lookup + `UNIQUE(stripePaymentIntentId)` | `lib/stripe-cards.ts:529`, `schema.prisma:416` |
815	
816	**Diagnosis.** For "why was I suspended": read `Server.dunningStage`, `dunningNextAt`,
817	`suspendReason` and `suspendedNote`, then the `AuditLog` rows (`billing.suspended_unpaid`) and
818	`EmailLog` for the four dunning templates. For "the card was charged but nothing happened": look up
819	the PaymentIntent by marker `renew:<serverId>:<periodStart>` in Stripe and check for a
820	`WalletTransaction` with that `stripePaymentIntentId`.
821	
822	**Honest note — the biggest live gap in billing.** The engine is real and wired
823	(`worker/billing.ts:28-43` imports 13 symbols from `lib/stripe-cards`), but **there is no UI for a
824	customer to save a card.** `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-payment-method.ts` exports `startCardSetup`
825	(`:46`), `finalizeCardSetup` (`:72`), `removeSavedCard` (`:101`) and `settleOutstanding` (`:127`),
826	and a repo-wide grep finds **zero callers** in `app/` or `components/`. So today the auto-charge path

828	goes straight to grace → suspend. The card-on-file card sketched in the Wallet chapter's wireframe is
829	what the engine expects, not what is rendered.

538	## Wallet, checkout and the wallet/card split
539	
540	**What it does.** Every customer has a single integer-cent balance, `User.balanceCents`. All
541	purchases debit the wallet; a card is used only to make up a shortfall. That inversion — wallet
542	first, card for the remainder — is the platform's core payment shape and it recurs in checkout,
543	resize, disk expansion and renewals.
544	
545	```
546	┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
547	│  Billing                                                              │
548	├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
549	│   WALLET BALANCE                            PAYMENT METHOD            │
550	│   ┌───────────────────────────────┐         ┌───────────────────────┐ │
551	│   │      $42.10                   │         │ VISA •••• 4242  09/29 │ │
552	│   │  [ Add funds ]                │         │ default    [Remove]   │ │
553	│   └───────────────────────────────┘         │ [ + Add a card ]      │ │
554	│                                             └───────────────────────┘ │
555	│   ADD FUNDS   ( )$10  ( )$25  (•)$50  ( )$100   ( ) custom            │
556	│               Coupon code [___________]  [Apply]                      │
557	│               [  Continue to payment  ]                               │
558	├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
559	│   TRANSACTIONS                                                        │
560	│   2026-07-24  Top-up (card)                            +$50.00        │
561	│   2026-07-24  Order web-01 — KVM 2, 24 mo              −$128.38       │
562	│   2026-07-20  Resize KVM 2 → KVM 4 (prorated)          −$61.02        │
563	└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
564	```
565	
566	**The split, exactly.** `/opt/nxeon/lib/wallet-split.ts` is a *pure, dependency-free* module —
567	deliberately importable by both client wizards and server actions, so the split the customer sees is
568	byte-for-byte the split that gets charged.
569	
570	```
571	 dueCents, balanceCents, useWallet
572	   │
573	   ├─ useWallet false ─────────────────► wallet 0        card = due
574	   ├─ balance ≥ due ───────────────────► wallet = due    card = 0   (no Stripe at all)
575	   ├─ balance < due ───────────────────► wallet = balance card = due − balance
576	   └─ 0 < card < STRIPE_MIN_CENTS(50) ─► wallet = due − 50, card = 50
577	      and dueCents ≥ 50                  clampedForStripeMin = true
578	                                         (Stripe rejects sub-$0.50 charges)
579	```
580	
581	**Fulfilment — the part that used to lose money.** Both the browser redirect and the Stripe webhook
582	call one shared function:
583	
584	```
585	 Stripe Checkout completed
586	   ├──► GET /api/stripe/confirm?session_id=…   (browser, may never happen)
587	   └──► POST /api/stripe/webhook               (server-to-server, reliable)
588	              │
589	              └─► fulfilCheckoutSession(sessionId)      lib/fulfil-checkout.ts
590	                    1. creditCheckoutSession()  — idempotent via
591	                       UNIQUE(WalletTransaction.stripeSessionId).
592	                       Its RETURN VALUE IS DELIBERATELY IGNORED.
593	                    2. claim(sessionId, kind) — INSERT FulfilledSession.
594	                       UNIQUE(stripeSessionId) picks the single winner.
595	                    3. winner runs placeOrder / applyResize / applyDiskExpand
596	                    4. settle(DONE|FAILED, detail)
597	                    on FAILED: money stays in the wallet + a Notification
598	                    "Payment received — we couldn't finish setting up your server"
599	```
600	
601	The header comment at `/opt/nxeon/lib/fulfil-checkout.ts:1-19` states the original bug: fulfilment
602	was gated on `creditCheckoutSession()` returning `true`, which is true only for whoever won the
603	*credit* race. If the webhook won, or the customer closed the tab, the card was charged, the wallet
604	credited, and no server was ever created — silently. `FulfilledSession`
605	(`prisma/schema.prisma:741`) exists solely to be its own idempotency marker rather than a side
606	effect of crediting.
607	
608	**Entry points.**
609	
610	| Concern | Location |
611	|---|---|
612	| Split maths (shared client + server) | `/opt/nxeon/lib/wallet-split.ts` |
613	| Debit / credit primitives | `/opt/nxeon/lib/wallet.ts` (`debitWallet`, `InsufficientBalanceError`) |
614	| Checkout session creation | `/opt/nxeon/app/api/stripe/checkout/route.ts` |
615	| Session → intent decoding, `chargeCents` metadata | `/opt/nxeon/lib/stripe.ts:52`, `:92`, `:123` |
616	| The one fulfilment path | `/opt/nxeon/lib/fulfil-checkout.ts` |
617	| Success redirect | `/opt/nxeon/app/api/stripe/confirm/route.ts` |
618	| Webhook | `/opt/nxeon/app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts` |
619	| Cards on file | `/opt/nxeon/lib/stripe-cards.ts` |
620	
621	**Data model.** `User.balanceCents`; `WalletTransaction` (`prisma/schema.prisma:411`) with
622	`stripeSessionId` UNIQUE (Checkout idempotency) and `stripePaymentIntentId` UNIQUE (off-session
623	renewal idempotency); `FulfilledSession` (`:741`) `kind` ∈ `order|resize|diskExpand|topup`,
624	`status` ∈ `CLAIMED|DONE|FAILED`.
625	
626	**Failure modes.**
627	
628	| Symptom | Cause | Where to look |
629	|---|---|---|
630	| Paid, no server, no error | The old confirm/webhook race — should be impossible now | `FulfilledSession` row for that session: `status: FAILED` + `detail` |
631	| Charged twice for one resize | Would require two Checkout sessions | `WalletTransaction` rows; UNIQUE constraints make a replay a no-op |
632	| "Insufficient balance" with money visible | Balance changed between quote and order | `WalletTransaction` ordering |
633	| Card declined at Stripe | Checkout never completes; no `FulfilledSession` row | Stripe dashboard |
634	
635	**Diagnosis.** Start from `FulfilledSession`: no row means Stripe never reported the session
636	complete; `CLAIMED` and stuck means fulfilment threw before settling; `FAILED` carries the reason in
637	`detail` (500 chars). Then reconcile `WalletTransaction` against the customer's balance.
638	
639	**Honest note.** Coupon codes on **card top-ups** were historically accepted, promised in the UI,
640	and silently ignored — the cookie was read only by the demo gateway, which refuses in production,
641	and the Stripe Checkout session carried no `discounts`. Verify current behaviour before telling a
642	customer a bonus will land; see Known gaps.
643	
644	## Invoices
645	
646	**What it does.** Produces a numbered, self-contained HTML billing document for orders, renewals,
647	resizes and disk expansions. There is no PDF renderer and no external template engine — the HTML is
648	built by string concatenation in `/opt/nxeon/lib/invoices.ts`.
649	
650	```
651	┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
652	│  Nxeon                                        INVOICE #00042  │
653	│                                               2026-07-24      │
654	│  Billed to                                    Status  PAID    │
655	│  alice@example.com                                            │
656	├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
657	│  Description                        Qty   Unit      Amount    │
658	│  ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  │
659	│  KVM 2 — 2 vCPU / 8 GB / 100 GB      24  $7.64    $183.40     │
660	│  Extra root disk 40 GB               24  $4.00     $96.00     │
661	│  Seasonal promo −30%                  1  −$83.82  −$83.82     │
662	│  ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  │
663	│                                     Subtotal      $195.58     │
664	│                                     Tax             $0.00     │
665	│                                     TOTAL         $195.58     │
666	└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
667	```
668	
669	**Entry points.** `invoiceCreateData()` builds the row (`/opt/nxeon/lib/invoices.ts:60` onward,
670	`amountCents = subtotalCents + taxCents` at `:83`); `invoiceTotals()` at `:36` recomputes for
671	display; the HTML document is rendered from `:145`, invoice number zero-padded to five digits at
672	`:147`. Customer view `/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/invoices/[id]/page.tsx`; admin view
673	`/opt/nxeon/app/admin/invoices/[id]/page.tsx`; CSV export
674	`/opt/nxeon/app/api/admin/export/route.ts:121`.
675	
676	Creators: `lib/order.ts` (orders), `lib/resize.ts:124` (one PAID invoice per user-initiated
677	resize), `lib/disk-expand.ts:172` (proration invoice whose line item spells out both the permanence
678	and the recurring monthly cost), `worker/billing.ts` (renewals).
679	
680	**Data model.** `Invoice` (`prisma/schema.prisma:510`): `number`, `status` (`InvoiceStatus` at
681	`:503`), `lineItems` JSON, `taxCents`, `amountCents`, `userId`.
682	
683	**Honest notes.**
684	
685	- **Tax is configured and never charged.** `tax_percent` is admin-editable and read by
686	  `/opt/nxeon/lib/tax.ts:73`, but `applyTaxFromSettings` has exactly one call site —
687	  `/opt/nxeon/app/admin/products/page.tsx:93`, an admin MRR display. No invoice creator passes
688	  `taxCents`, so every invoice has `taxCents = 0` and the "Tax" row always renders $0.00.
689	- **`invoice_prefix` is saved and read by nothing.** The admin can set it
690	  (`lib/settings.ts` default `"INV-"`); the renderer hardcodes `INVOICE #` and pads the number.
691	
692	## Renewals, card auto-charge and dunning

1686	## Server migration — cutover, re-runs and the missing TLS retry
1687	
1688	**DNS repointing is manual, customer-initiated, one click per hostname.** The engine never touches
1689	DNS.
1690	
1691	```
1692	 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
1693	 │  Point your domains at the new server                               │
1694	 ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
1695	 │  studionexis.com        registered with Nxeon    → 51.79.162.96     │
1696	 │                                                     [ Point now ]   │
1697	 │  content.example.ca     found on the new server     [ Point now ]   │
1698	 │  stg.example.com        from the old server's vhosts  ✗ NOT SERVING │
1699	 │                         do not move DNS for this name yet           │
1700	 │                                                                     │
1701	 │  Or roll back: point the A record at your old server.               │
1702	 │  [ Open Cloudflare DNS ↗ ]                                          │
1703	 └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
1704	```
1705	
1706	Candidates come from three sources — `getMigrationDnsInfo()` at `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-migrate.ts:743`:
1707	`Domain` rows registered with Nxeon (`:764`), `Website` rows on the target (`:772`), and hostnames
1708	inferred from the **stored** scan snapshot's web-root folder names (`:779`). It explicitly never
1709	re-scans the source (`:741`).
1710	
1711	The write is `pointMigrationDns()` at `:804` → `pointHostnameToIp` (`lib/cloudflare-point.ts:97`).
1712	Cloudflare only. A **single DNS-only A record**, `proxied: false` — which is load-bearing: an orange-
1713	clouded record breaks HTTP-01 validation, and HTTP-01 is the only challenge the SSL subsystem uses
1714	(`lib/cloudflare-point.ts:12-17`, `:158-162`).
1715	
1716	**Cloudflare is involved three ways:** the A-record write above; **DNS-01 wildcard issuance** — a
1717	`*.domain` certificate cannot be issued any other way, so `resolveTlsInputs()`
1718	(`worker/migrate.ts:186`) resolves the customer's token and passes it as `cloudflareToken` (`:389`) to
1719	`secureSites` rung 3 (`migrate-real.ts:3125`) → `issueDns01` (`:2991`); and a deep link for manual
1720	rollback (`MigrationWizard.tsx:1596`).
1721	
1722	**How an admin re-runs a failed migration: there is no re-run path.** Verified:
1723	
1724	- No admin UI. `db.migration` is referenced only in `lib/actions-migrate.ts`; there is no
1725	  `app/admin/**` migration page at all.
1726	- No retry action. The exported actions are `createMigration` (`:324`), `scanSource` (`:461`),

2707	   │  monitoring     servers:read     never used            [🗑]   │

2721	(`prisma/schema.prisma:906`) — tokens are `nxe_…`, stored sha256-hashed.

2724	`servers:*`, or the generic `read` which satisfies any `*:read`.

2737	## Two-factor authentication — and why `lib/totp-verify.ts` is a plain module
2738	
2739	**What it does.** RFC 6238 TOTP with hashed one-time backup codes, challenged at login, plus an
2740	admin-settable requirement for staff.
2741	
2742	```
2743	 LOGIN
2744	  ├─ 1. rate limit: login_ratelimit_max (default 10) per 15 min per email+IP
2745	  │        lib/actions.ts:150
2746	  ├─ 2. password check
2747	  ├─ 3. if user.totpEnabled → 2FA challenge     lib/actions.ts:166
2748	  │        verifyTotpForUser(userId, code)      lib/totp-verify.ts:50
2749	  │          ├─ verifyTOTP(secret, code)                  → pass
2750	  │          └─ else consume a matching backup code       → pass, code removed
2751	  └─ 4. session cookie, session_length_days (default 30)   lib/auth.ts
2752	```
2753	
2754	**This is the most instructive security story in the codebase.** `verifyTotpForUser` used to live in
2755	`lib/actions-2fa.ts`, which carries `"use server"` at the top. **Every export of such a module is a
2756	registered, network-callable server action.** The docblock at `/opt/nxeon/lib/totp-verify.ts:6-23`
2757	spells out what that meant:
2758	
2759	> That made this function a public endpoint taking an arbitrary `userId`, performing no
2760	> authentication, no ownership check and no rate limiting, returning a raw boolean — and mutating
2761	> state, because a matching backup code is consumed. `login()` is throttled to 10 attempts per 15
2762	> minutes per email+IP; calling this action directly bypassed that completely, allowing **unlimited
2763	> TOTP and backup-code guessing against a named account**. Victim user IDs were obtainable from the
2764	> team page.
2765	
2766	So `lib/totp-verify.ts` is **deliberately a plain module**. It has no `"use server"`, which means there
2767	is no action ID for a client to call — it can only be reached by server code that imports it. There
2768	are exactly two importers: `lib/actions-2fa.ts:10` (the management actions) and `lib/actions.ts:28`
2769	(the login flow). The file ends with an instruction: **"Do NOT re-export any of this from a
2770	`"use server"` module."** Honour it.
2771	
2772	The function itself carries the matching contract (`:44-48`): callers **must** have already established
2773	that the request is entitled to attempt a 2FA check for this user, and **must** apply their own rate
2774	limiting — *"this function deliberately has neither, which is precisely why it must never be exposed as
2775	a server action."*
2776

2778	`totpSecretOf` `:33`, `verifyTotpForUser` `:50`), `lib/actions-2fa.ts` (enrol, disable, regenerate
2779	codes), `lib/actions.ts:150` (throttle) and `:166` (challenge). Secrets are stored encrypted
2780	(`totpSecretEnc`) with a legacy plaintext fallback so already-enrolled users keep working
2781	(`totp-verify.ts:33`). Backup codes are sha256-hashed and consumption is audit-logged
2782	(`user.2fa_backup_code_used`, `:63`). Staff enforcement: `enforce_staff_2fa`, read by
2783	`app/admin/layout.tsx`. Tests: `/opt/nxeon/test/totp.test.ts`, `/opt/nxeon/test/rate-limit.test.ts`.

export const STRIPE_METADATA_VALUE_MAX = 500;

/**
 * Serialise a payload for Stripe metadata, refusing rather than truncating.
 *
 * WHY THIS EXISTS. Every one of these payloads used to be written as
 * `JSON.stringify(x).slice(0, 490)`. A slice through JSON produces a string that
 * is no longer JSON, and the consumer's `JSON.parse` throws inside a `try` that
 * returns `null` on failure — at which point `fulfilCheckoutSession` cannot see an
 * order, a resize or a disk expansion in the session, and falls through to its
 * plain wallet-top-up branch. The customer's card is charged, the money lands in
 * their wallet, **no server is created, no error is shown and no failure row is
 * written**. Silent, and invisible from every surface we own.
 *
 * The correct behaviour was already argued for elsewhere in this file, about the
 * card leg: "Refuse to open a session rather than take the money and discover it
 * at confirm time — nothing has been charged at this point." That reasoning
 * applies identically here, so it is applied identically. Throwing happens BEFORE
 * `checkout.sessions.create`, so the customer sees a failure on a page where they
 * have paid nothing, which is the cheapest possible moment to fail.
 *
 * Never re-introduce a slice here. If a payload legitimately outgrows the cap, the
 * fix is to persist it and put a key in metadata — never to send half of it.
 */
export function packMetadata(label: string, payload: unknown): string {
  const json = JSON.stringify(payload);
  if (json.length > STRIPE_METADATA_VALUE_MAX) {
    throw new Error(
      `${label} is ${json.length} characters, over Stripe's ${STRIPE_METADATA_VALUE_MAX}-character metadata limit. ` +
        `Refusing to create a payment session rather than send a truncated payload that would take the money and ` +
        `provision nothing.`,
    );
  }
  return json;
}

/**
 * Create a Checkout session that pays for a VPS order directly (no wallet pre-fund).
 *
 * `amountCents` is the CARD leg only (the remainder after wallet credit); the FULL
 * order total rides along in metadata as `nxeonOrderPrice` so the confirm route can
 * settle the price this order was SOLD at instead of re-pricing it once the card
 * has already cleared. That re-pricing — and the silent wallet draw that paid for
 * it — is the H2 incident described on `OrderPrice` in lib/order.ts.
 *
 * `sold` lets the caller hand in the very quote it split the payment from, so the
 * card leg and the stamped total are two halves of ONE pricing. When it is omitted
 * the order is priced here, once, at the moment the session is created — still
 * before any money moves, which is the property that matters.
 */

488	## Plans, terms and pricing
489	
490	**What it does.** A `Plan` is a CPU/RAM/disk/bandwidth tier with one monthly price. A **term**
491	applies a commitment discount on top. A **promo** applies a seasonal discount on top of that.
492	
493	Term ladder — `/opt/nxeon/lib/billing-terms.ts:9`:
494	
495	| Term | `months` | Discount | $8.99/mo plan → effective |
496	|---|---|---|---|
497	| Monthly | 1 | 0% | $8.99/mo |
498	| Annual | 12 | 10% | $8.09/mo |
499	| Biennial | 24 | 15% | $7.64/mo |
500	| Triennial | 36 | 20% | $7.19/mo |
501	
502	Domains have their own ladder (`DOMAIN_TERMS`, 1/2/3 years at 0/5/10%).
503	
504	The three pricing functions, and this is the whole contract:
505	
506	```
507	vpsTermPriceCents(monthly, months)   = round(monthly × months × (1 − disc))
508	                                       → what is CHARGED
509	vpsEffectiveMonthly(monthly, months) = round(termPrice / months)
510	                                       → what is DISPLAYED as "$/mo"
511	promoPriceCents(cents, promo)        = seasonal discount on top   lib/promotions.ts
512	```
513	
514	Renewals bill `vpsTermPriceCents` **unchanged** — the promo applies to the first term only. That is
515	stated in the comment at `/opt/nxeon/lib/order.ts:130`.
516	
517	**Entry points.** Term table and maths `/opt/nxeon/lib/billing-terms.ts`; promo
518	`/opt/nxeon/lib/promotions.ts` (`promoPriceCents` at `:127`, `currentPromo`); admin plan CRUD
519	`/opt/nxeon/app/admin/plans`; catalog seed `/opt/nxeon/prisma/catalog.ts`; the one test that guards
520	this is `/opt/nxeon/test/billing-terms.test.ts`.
521	
522	**Data model.** `Plan` (`prisma/schema.prisma:253`): `slug`, `cpuCores`, `ramMB`, `diskGB`,
523	`bandwidthTB`, `priceCents`, `storageTier` (`nvme` | `hdd`), `active`, `sortOrder`. `GamePlan`
524	(`:777`) layers a game tier on top of a base `Plan`. `Server.termMonths` records which term was
525	bought.
526	
527	**Failure mode that actually happened.** The wizard displayed $8.99 and charged $6.29 because the
528	promo was applied on one side only. Both sides now apply it — but by *duplication*, not by sharing
529	one function: `promoPriceCents` is reimplemented client-side in the wizard rather than imported.
530	There is still **no server-side `expectedCents` binding**, so a wizard left open across a promo
531	boundary, or an admin price change mid-session, can still charge something other than what was on
532	screen. See Known gaps.
533	
534	**Diagnosis.** For "I was charged the wrong amount": read the `Invoice.lineItems` (they spell out
535	term and promo), then re-run the maths by hand with `vpsTermPriceCents` and the promo that was live
536	at `Invoice.createdAt`. `AuditLog` action `server.order` records `plan=`, `term=`, `extraDisk=`.
